chunks: From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakam, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sells an item, and the buyer says it is for such and such an amount less than what the seller said, he (the Imam) said: 'The word is the word of the seller if the item is still present with his oath.'

key_terms.قَائِمًا بِعَيْنِهِ: Still present/existing in its original state

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on price negotiation in Islam when the buyer offers less than the asking price?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of offer and acceptance (*ijab wa qabul*) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the seller retains the final authority to bind the contract until they explicitly swear an oath to the new price. It highlights the principle that mere counter-offering does not dissolve the original offer, preserving the seller's right of revocation (*khiyar*) while the goods remain in their possession. This ruling underscores the importance of clear intent and verbal commitment in commercial transactions to prevent ambiguity.
